The train yard at OMF Central in Seattle’s SODO neighborhood features artwork called “Safety Spires,” by Norie Sato and Dan Corson. Through color and a simple pattern, Sato and Corson transformed the facility’s overhead catenary system poles into a collection of horsetail reeds.
The 160,000-square-foot OMF Central in SODO includes nine service bays, a repair center, and automated wash-bays like an oversized car wash facility.
Each Link OMF creates hundreds of permanent high-skilled, living wage jobs.
The LEED Gold-certified OMF East in Bellevue opened in 2021. The facility includes rooftop solar panels to offset energy use, a water capture system, and public art along a popular public bike path.
Sound Transit’s expert technicians and maintenance teams work 24 hours a day, 365 days a year to ensure safe, clean, and reliable Link service.
